Fact.Name: Activities requiring Form 6198 detail
Fact.Description: One activity per Form 6198 copy. Schedule C, Schedule E, and Schedule F keep their current activity facts; this collection is the form's reporting surface pending a shared activity identity.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 activity copies to render
Fact.Description: Activity entries that incurred a line-5 loss; one Form 6198 is rendered for each such activity.

Fact.Name: Return files Form 6198
Fact.Description:
True when at least one modeled activity incurred a line-5 loss. The Switch guard counts the activities whose decision inputs are complete against the activities whose decision-input fact resolves at all, and answers only when the two counts agree, so one activity with an unanswered line 5 withholds the aggregate rather than answering false. An empty collection is complete-false.
THE ABSENT COLLECTION IS ALSO COMPLETE-FALSE, and that took the first Case. Every ordinary return leaves /form6198Activities UNANSWERED — not [] — and a bare Count over an unanswered collection is a PLACEHOLDER, so this return-level fact resolved Placeholder(false) rather than Complete(false) on every return that has never seen an at-risk activity. Measured, not read: tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-absent-activities failed with "completeness Placeholder, want Complete" before the guard. The value was never wrong; the completeness was, and a Placeholder is not an answer a return-level filing decision may give. It matters because an absent collection is the state of the entire population.
The three states are now all pinned: ABSENT -> Complete false (-absent-activities), [] -> Complete false (-empty-activities), one unanswered line 5 among several activities -> Incomplete (-two-activities-one-incomplete).

Fact.Name: Form 6198 activity description
Fact.Description: Identify the activity whose profit, loss, and amount at risk are reported on this copy.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 1 ordinary income or loss
Fact.Description: Ordinary income or loss from the activity.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 2a Schedule D gain or loss
Fact.Description: Gain or loss from an activity asset disposition reported on Schedule D.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 2b Form 4797 gain or loss
Fact.Description: Gain or loss from an activity asset disposition reported on Form 4797.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 2c other disposition gain or loss
Fact.Description: Gain or loss from an activity asset disposition reported on another form or schedule.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 3 other Schedule K-1 income and gains
Fact.Description: Other activity income and gains from Schedule K-1 not already included on lines 1 through 2c.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 4 other deductions and losses
Fact.Description: Enter the positive deduction or loss amount not already included on lines 1 through 2c; the form prints this amount in parentheses.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 5 current-year activity profit or loss
Fact.Description: Combine lines 1 through 4, subtracting line 4's positive deduction magnitude.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 6 beginning adjusted basis
Fact.Description: Adjusted basis in the activity at the beginning of the tax year; the form does not permit an amount below zero.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 7 current-year increases
Fact.Description: Increase in the amount at risk for the tax year under the Form 6198 instructions.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 8 basis plus increases
Fact.Description: Add lines 6 and 7.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 9 current-year decreases
Fact.Description: Decrease in the amount at risk for the tax year under the Form 6198 instructions.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 10a amount at risk after decreases
Fact.Description: Subtract line 9 from line 8.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 10b simplified amount at risk
Fact.Description: Line 10a when positive; otherwise zero.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 11 investment at effective date
Fact.Description: Investment in the activity at its effective date for the detailed computation.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 12 effective-date increases
Fact.Description: Increases at the effective date for the detailed amount-at-risk computation.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 13 investment plus increases
Fact.Description: Add lines 11 and 12.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 14 effective-date decreases
Fact.Description: Decreases at the effective date for the detailed amount-at-risk computation.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 15 beginning amount at risk
Fact.Description: Enter the amount from line 13 less line 14, or the prior-year Form 6198 line 19b amount, as applicable. The Part III checkbox choice remains a register gap.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 16 increases since effective date or prior year end
Fact.Description: Increases since the effective date or the end of the prior year, depending on the activity's Part III method. The checkbox choice remains a register gap.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 17 amount before later decreases
Fact.Description: Add lines 15 and 16.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 18 decreases since effective date or prior year end
Fact.Description: Decreases since the effective date or the end of the prior year. The checkbox choice remains a register gap.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 19a detailed amount at risk before floor
Fact.Description: Subtract line 18 from line 17.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 19b detailed amount at risk
Fact.Description: Line 19a when positive; otherwise zero.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 20 amount at risk
Fact.Description:
"Amount at risk. Enter the larger of line 10b or line 19b" — the printed line, computed. A free writable here would let the form print "the larger of line 10b or line 19b" beside two computed zeros and a typed $1,200 on the branch's own witness; the witness REACHES $1,200 from line 6, which is what the published example means.
GUARDED, because Part II and Part III are alternatives and the printed form picks between them with checkboxes this module does not yet hold (lines 16 and 18, Part III's "effective date / end of prior year" pair, are declared register gaps). So: * both legs resolve -> the larger, exactly as printed; * only Part II answered -> line 10b, because an unfilled Part III is not a $0 Part III; * only Part III answered -> line 19b, the mirror of the same reading; * neither -> Incomplete. No silent $0, and line 21 stays Incomplete with it. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-line20-larger-of-19b (19b $1,500 beats 10b $1,200), -part3-unanswered (19b Incomplete, line 20 falls to 10b $1,200) and -neither-part-answered (both Incomplete, line 20 and line 21 Incomplete).
THE FOURTH §465 INTAKE IS RETIRED WITH THE WRITABLE. scheduleC (/scheduleCs/*/writableAmountAtRisk), scheduleF (/writableScheduleFAmountAtRisk) and scheduleE (/formK1s/*/atRiskActivityShares/*/writableActivityAmountAtRisk) already ask the filer for an amount at risk; this module asked a fourth time for the same activity. What those three hold is a per-ACTIVITY figure this module cannot read — none of them is exported and the activity identifier is not shared — and that shared-identity hook is the recorded successor, not a fourth writable.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 21 deductible loss
Fact.Description: The smaller of the positive line-5 loss magnitude or line 20. Exported as the successor for Schedule C/E/F at-risk loss allowances.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 total of the activity's loss items
Fact.Description:
The total of the deduction and loss items entered in Part I: the magnitude of each negative amount on lines 1, 2a, 2b and 2c, plus line 4, which the form already takes as a positive deduction.
THIS IS THE FRACTION'S DENOMINATOR, and which total it is decides the whole allocation. The instructions call it "the total loss from the activity on line 5", which reads at first like the NET on line 5. It is not. The line-5 passage settles it: there the same fraction is used to multiply the total income and gains, which only works when the fractions sum to one, and they sum to one only over the items' total. Read as the net, a single loss item standing against a gain would take a share LARGER than the whole allowed loss on line 21. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-line21-allocation-gain-offset: a $4,600 loss item against a $3,100 gain, net line 5 of -$1,500, and the item's share is the whole of line 21.
THE IRS'S OWN WORKED EXAMPLE SETTLES IT, and it is the reason this is no longer only a fixture argument. The published Line 5 example is a $4,600 Schedule C loss on line 1 against a $3,100 Schedule D gain on line 2a, line 5 a loss of $1,500, and the filer "can deduct $3,100 of the $4,600 loss on Schedule C". The paragraph's rule is: divide each deduction or loss by the total loss, then multiply the total income and gains by that fraction. Over the loss items the fraction is 4,600 / 4,600 = 1 and 1 x $3,100 = $3,100 — the published answer. Over the net it is 4,600 / 1,500 and the same step yields $9,506, which the IRS does not print. The gain-offset fixture reproduces exactly this example.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 21 share of the ordinary loss
Fact.Description:
Line 1's ordinary loss from the activity's share of the allowed loss on line 21: line 21 multiplied by this item's magnitude over the total of the loss items. Zero when the activity has no loss item.
NOT "the amount of this item allowed". The item's total allowable deduction is this share PLUS the portion absorbed against the activity's own income and gains under the separate line-5 method, which this module does not compute. Naming these facts a share and not an allowance is deliberate: with income or a gain in Part I the two differ, and form6198-line21-allocation-gain-offset is exactly such a case.
The remainder of each item is disallowed and carried over item by item; this module carries the remainder over only in total (activityDisallowedLossCarriedToNextYear), because a per-item carryover has no reader — no dictionary module reads /form6198Activities at all.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 line 21 allocation rounding residual
Fact.Description:
Line 21 less the five item shares. It is zero whenever the fraction divides evenly and a cent or two otherwise.
DECLARED LIMIT: THE FIVE SHARES THEMSELVES DO NOT SUM TO LINE 21. Five shares rounded to cents need not sum to the total they came from, and the instructions prescribe NO reconciliation rule — no residual item, no largest-remainder rule, no "adjust the largest share". Any rule this module invented to make them add up would be an invention with a dollar consequence per item, so it invents none: it exports the difference and names it. A reader that must make the shares add up has the number to do it with, and the choice of WHERE to put it is that reader's, not this module's. Pinned at 0.00 by form6198-line21-allocation-exact and form6198-line21-allocation-rounds (both divide evenly at the cent), and at 0.01 by form6198-line21-allocation-residual — three equal $100 items against a $100 line 21, each share $33.33, the shares summing to $99.99. That last fixture is the witness that this fact is not always zero.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 disallowed loss carried to next year
Fact.Description:
The part of this activity's line-5 loss that the at-risk limit disallowed: the loss magnitude less the allowed amount on line 21, floored at zero.
The statute makes the disallowed remainder a deduction of the FIRST SUCCEEDING year, and the instructions say the same about each item. The form itself points at it — its deductible-loss caption sends the filer to the instructions "to find out how to report any deductible loss and any carryover" — but this module held no such fact, while Schedules E and F and Form 4835 all expose their own suspended at-risk loss. This closes that asymmetry.
NOT FOLDED IN, and named so no one mistakes this for the whole carryover: the second component, the amount recaptured into income under 465(e)(1)(A), which that paragraph's (B) makes a deduction of the next year as well. It is exported separately as section465eRecaptureIncome. Nothing in the dictionary reads either yet; what is missing is a shared activity identity, not this fact.

Fact.Name: Total deduction allocable to this activity next year
Fact.Description:
The two amounts the statute makes a deduction of the FIRST SUCCEEDING year for this activity, added: the loss the at-risk limit disallowed, and the amount recaptured into gross income because the amount at risk ended the year below zero.
They are separate paragraphs and separate facts, and they are kept separate because they have different characters downstream; this fact exists because the reader that carries an activity forward wants one number, and computing it here beats every reader re-deriving it. Incomplete whenever either half is Incomplete — a total of a known amount and an unknown one is not the known one. Pinned at $400.00, $2,100.00 and Incomplete by tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-published-line21-example, -recapture-cap-not-binding and -recapture-part2-below-zero.

Fact.Name: Amount at risk at the close of the year, before the printed floor
Fact.Description:
The activity's amount at risk at the close of the tax year WITHOUT the floor the form prints. It mirrors the printed larger-of choice exactly as line 20 does, but over the unfloored 10a and 19a instead of 10b and 19b, so it can be negative.
Why it exists: 10b and 19b are where the form says "Otherwise, enter -0- and see Pub. 925 for information on the recapture rules". The floor is a printing rule; the statute asks whether zero EXCEEDS the amount at risk at the close of the year, and after the floor that question can no longer be asked. GUARDED the same way line 20 is, and for the same reason: both legs -> the larger; one leg -> that leg, because an unfilled Part is not a zero Part; neither -> Incomplete.
DECLARED LIMIT, AND THE DIRECTION OF ITS RISK IS UNDER-CHARGE. No source picks the LARGER of the two unfloored amounts. The printed larger-of on line 20 is a choice between two amounts the form has already floored at zero, where "larger" means "more loss allowed"; applied BEFORE the floor to two NEGATIVE amounts, "larger" means "the smaller recapture", which is the taxpayer-favourable direction and the harmful one if it is wrong. The printed form attaches the recapture pointer to each Part independently — 10b and 19b each say "Otherwise, enter -0- and see Pub. 925 for information on the recapture rules" — and says nothing about combining them. Mirroring line 20 is chosen for internal consistency (one method decides both the loss limit and the recapture) and is DECLARED, not derived. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-recapture-both-parts-negative: Part II -$500 against Part III -$900 yields an excess of $500, not $900. That fixture pins a DECLARED LIMIT and goes RED if a ruling picks the more negative leg.
NEEDS-SOURCE, twice over, because Pub. 925 is not vendored in sources/ and nothing here rests on it: (a) whether 465(e) measures the amount at risk at the same point as the form's 10a/19a — which is the figure BEFORE the current year's allowed loss reduces it, the instructions' own CAUTION being that the PRIOR year's line 21 loss reduces the at-risk investment as of the START of the current year; and (b) the combining rule above. Both are exactly what Pub. 925's recapture discussion covers.

Fact.Name: Amount by which zero exceeds the year-end amount at risk
Fact.Description: Zero less the year-end amount at risk, floored at zero: the excess the statute includes in gross income. Zero for every activity that ends the year at or above zero, which is every activity this form is normally filed for.

Fact.Name: Prior-year at-risk reductions for this activity
Fact.Description: The total by which losses of prior tax years beginning after 1978 reduced the amount at risk in this activity. It is the first half of the statutory cap on recapture and is asked only of a filer whose amount at risk ended the year below zero.

Fact.Name: Recapture already included in income for this activity
Fact.Description: The amounts already taken into gross income for this activity under the same recapture paragraph in earlier years. It is the second half of the statutory cap, subtracted from the prior-year reductions so nothing is recaptured twice.

Fact.Name: At-risk recapture included in gross income for this activity
Fact.Description:
The smaller of the below-base excess (/form6198Activities/*/section465eRecaptureExcessAfterPre1979Base, which is the below-zero excess except for a pre-1979 activity) and the statutory cap (prior-year at-risk reductions less amounts already recaptured, floored at zero).
This fact is HALF of the section 465(e) recapture. The other half is not in this module's gift: nothing adds this amount to gross income, because no module reads /form6198Activities at all. Until a hub adds it, a filer whose amount at risk ends the year below zero is still under-charged. This fact is the hook that fix will read, and the direction is recorded here so the omission is not silent.
COMPLETE-SAFETY, deliberate and pinned. The first Case answers $0 whenever the excess is zero and NEVER touches the two prior-year writables, so no ordinary return — every return whose amount at risk ends at or above zero — becomes Incomplete because these questions exist. Only a return that actually has a below-zero amount at risk waits on them, and waiting is right there: a cap of an unknown size is not a cap of zero. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-published-line21-example (excess $0, the writables absent, $0.00 out), -recapture-part2-below-zero (excess $500, the writables absent, Incomplete), -recapture-cap-not-binding ($500) and -recapture-cap-binding ($300).

Fact.Name: This activity's amount at risk was below zero at the end of the 1978 tax year
Fact.Description: ASK: "Was your amount at risk in this activity less than zero at the end of your tax year that began in 1978?" HELP: this matters only for an activity you have held since before 1979; for such an activity the recapture test compares the year-end amount at risk with that 1978 negative amount instead of with zero. ASKED WHEN: this activity's amount at risk ends the year below zero (/form6198Activities/*/section465eRecaptureExcess is more than $0). UNANSWERED: read as No, which is the answer for every activity that began after 1978. VALIDATION: Boolean. FEEDS /form6198Activities/*/section465eRecaptureBase: a Yes asks /form6198Activities/*/writableAtRiskAmountAtEndOf1978 and the recapture test compares the year-end amount at risk with that amount.

Fact.Name: This activity's amount at risk at the end of the 1978 tax year
Fact.Description: ASK: "What was your amount at risk in this activity at the end of your tax year that began in 1978? Enter it as a negative number." HELP: the recapture test for an activity held since before 1979 compares this year's ending amount at risk with this 1978 amount instead of with zero; if the 1978 amount was minus $50, losses are recaptured only when the amount at risk goes below minus $50. ASKED WHEN: /form6198Activities/*/writableAtRiskBelowZeroAtEndOf1978 is Yes. UNANSWERED: the recapture for this activity stays unresolved (a Yes with no amount is not a zero). VALIDATION: Dollar; an entry above zero is read as zero, since only a negative 1978 amount replaces zero.

Fact.Name: The 1978 question is answered Yes
Fact.Description: TRUE only when /form6198Activities/*/writableAtRiskBelowZeroAtEndOf1978 is answered Yes. An unanswered question reads as No, the answer for every activity that began after 1978, so this fact is always complete.

Fact.Name: The amount the section 465(e) recapture test measures against
Fact.Description: Zero, except for an activity held since before 1979 whose amount at risk was below zero at the end of the 1978 tax year (/form6198Activities/*/writableAtRiskBelowZeroAtEndOf1978 Yes): then that negative 1978 amount (/form6198Activities/*/writableAtRiskAmountAtEndOf1978, floored at zero from above, so a positive entry reads as zero). Incomplete on a Yes with no amount. An unanswered Yes/No reads as No, the answer for every activity that began after 1978.

Fact.Name: Amount by which the recapture base exceeds the year-end amount at risk
Fact.Description: /form6198Activities/*/section465eRecaptureBase less the year-end amount at risk, floored at zero: the excess the statute includes in gross income once the pre-1979 substitution is applied. Equal to /form6198Activities/*/section465eRecaptureExcess on every activity whose base is zero, and never larger than it, because the base is never above zero.

Fact.Name: This activity's section 465(e) recapture rests on a choice no vendored source settles
Fact.Description:
TRUE when this activity owes a recapture (/form6198Activities/*/section465eRecaptureExcess more than $0) AND the amount of that recapture depends on one of two choices the statute, the Form 6198 instructions and Pub. 925 leave unsettled here:
(1) A CURRENT-YEAR PROFIT (line 5 more than $0). Line 7 is told not to include the current year income or gains shown on lines 1 through 3, so line 10a is the amount at risk BEFORE the current year's income, and /form6198Activities/*/amountAtRiskAtYearEndBeforeFloor reads it. The statute measures at the close of the year, and whether the year's own income lifts that amount before the test is not stated in any vendored source. On a loss year the question does not arise: a negative amount at risk allows no loss, so the amount before and after the allowed loss is the same.
(2) BOTH PARTS NEGATIVE (lines 10a and 19a both answered and both below $0). The printed larger-of on line 20 is mirrored onto the two unfloored amounts, which on two negative amounts picks the SMALLER recapture; the form attaches its recapture pointer to each Part separately and says nothing about combining them.
Every other recapture - a loss or break-even year measured on one Part, or on two Parts of which at most one is negative, including a pre-1979 activity measured against its 1978 negative amount (/form6198Activities/*/section465eRecaptureBase) - is computed as the statute and Pub. 925 state it and still files. COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: each conjunction reads the completeness of its operands first, and an All short-circuits on a Complete-false operand, so an activity whose recapture inputs are unanswered resolves false here and waits on the recapture figure itself.

Fact.Name: Knockout: an at-risk recapture whose amount rests on a choice no source settles
Fact.Description: Blocks submission when any Form 6198 activity owes a section 465(e) recapture whose amount depends on a current-year profit or on two negative Parts (/form6198Activities/*/recaptureRestsOnAnUnsourcedChoice). SCREEN: "This return includes an at-risk activity whose amount at risk ended the year below zero in a way this product cannot yet figure: the activity had a profit this year, both the simplified and the detailed computations of the amount at risk are below zero. The recaptured amount depends on rules the IRS instructions do not spell out, so this return cannot be filed here. A tax professional can figure the recapture from Pub. 925." A return with no at-risk activity, and every recapture outside those two populations, is unaffected. DEFERRAL, not a permanent refusal: the computation that would retire it is not built. COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: an unanswered or empty activity list reads false before the count is taken, and every member of the count is complete-safe.

Fact.Name: This activity requires Form 6198
Fact.Description:
True when the activity incurred a line-5 loss.
This fact does not add a second test — that the loss also EXCEED line 20 — because that test is in no source. Who Must File names two conditions, a loss and some amount not at risk, and the second one is what puts an activity in this collection at all, so it is not re-tested here. The line 21 example (a) settles the direction: a $400 loss against $1,000 at risk is a FILED form, and the old gate refused it. There is no dollar effect — line 21 is read by no other module — but the attachment and the filed-return count were understated.
STILL NARROWER THAN THE SOURCE — THREE DECLARED LIMITS, each awaiting a ruling, none of them the law:
(1) DECLARED LIMIT, profit attachment. The line 5 instructions say a current-year PROFIT must "Also attach Form 6198", and this gate is false for a profit. Pinned as the false arm by tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-filegate-current-year-profit. That fixture pins a DECLARED LIMIT AWAITING A RULING, not the law: if the ruling says every entered activity files, that fixture goes RED and is re-pinned true.
(2) DECLARED LIMIT, the second filing trigger. Who Must File carries a SECOND, loss- independent trigger — an activity included in (6) under At-Risk Activities together with amounts borrowed as described in (3) under Amounts Not at Risk — and an exception for a filer whose only such borrowing predates May 4, 2004. Neither is modeled: this gate tests the loss alone, so an activity in (6) with no loss is not flagged.
(3) DECLARED LIMIT, the "amounts not at risk" condition. Who Must File names TWO conditions, a loss and some amount not at risk. There is NO attestation fact for the second one anywhere in this module or the dictionary; being entered in /form6198Activities is taken to BE that condition. That is an intake convention this dictionary declares, not something a source states, and the application owns the screen that makes it true.
Line 5 exactly zero is neither a loss nor a profit and is pinned false by tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-filegate-break-even.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 filing decision inputs complete
Fact.Description:
Complete when this activity's line 5 profit or loss is known.
It does not require line 20, which would make /form6198ReturnFilesThisForm withhold its answer for a filer who has entered the activity's income and deductions but not yet any Part II or Part III amount (pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-line20-neither-part-answered). Who Must File does not consult the amount at risk, so neither does the decision.

Fact.Name: Form 6198 decision-input completeness fact is resolved
Fact.Description:
True for each entered Form 6198 activity because its companion decision-input fact resolves to a complete Boolean even when the source amount is unanswered. This counts every activity against the count of activities whose required line 5 input is complete. (It said "line 5 and line 20" until the FILEGATE narrowing retired the line 20 leg; the text was stale, the arithmetic was not.)
COUNT COUNTS THE TRUE ELEMENTS, not the resolved ones: CountOperator increments only when the element is true. Read in the core, and WITNESSED — but by the Then side of the Switch, not by this pair. tests/nodes/ty2025/form6198/form6198-filegate-current-year-profit and -filegate-break-even each hold ONE activity whose activityRequiresForm is Complete FALSE, and both assert /form6198ReturnFilesThisForm false. A Count that counted elements would make that Count 1, and 1 is greater than 0, so the gate would say the return files.
A CORRECTION, since an earlier draft of this Description claimed otherwise: -two-activities-one-incomplete does NOT witness the counting rule. What it witnesses is the WITHHOLDING outcome — one of two activities with line 4 unanswered leaves the return-level fact Incomplete rather than answering over half a return — and that outcome survives whichever way the guard is read (see the next paragraph).
THIS PAIR IS BELT-AND-BRACES TODAY, AND THAT IS MEASURED. Replacing the count guard with an unconditional True leaves every committed fixture GREEN (review mutation A6, the only survivor of 23): CountOperator itself returns Incomplete as soon as any element is Incomplete, and activityRequiresForm is Incomplete exactly when its line 5 is, so the two routes agree on every input this module can be given. They part company only if activityRequiresForm stops depending on line 5 — which is precisely what the pending profit-attachment ruling would do, by making it a constant — or over a PLACEHOLDER line 5, which no writable here can produce. The guard is kept for the first of those, not deleted as dead code, and this paragraph is why.
